question: Assume today is 2026-08-16. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of foreign visitor arrivals to Japan in August 2026, as it will be first reported in the Japan National Tourism Organization's (JNTO) monthly estimate.

target.what: Preliminary JNTO monthly estimate of foreign visitor arrivals to Japan for August 2026: foreign nationals entering Japan during 1–31 August 2026, counted as visitor arrivals/entries in the headline JNTO series, not unique persons and not Japanese nationals.
target.cadence: Monthly; preliminary estimate usually first published in the following month (mid-September 2026 for August 2026).
target.caveats: Target period is ongoing at the 2026-08-16 cutoff, so only first-half August and forward-looking signals are available. The first-reported figure is preliminary and may be revised. The headline counts arrivals/visits rather than unique people; exact treatment of re-entry, transit, crew and cruise/se

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 can be projected from JNTO's own history: August 2025 level multiplied by recent year-on-year growth in Jan–Jul 2026, adjusted for calendar/Obon timing and market mix. Role: central baseline and seasonal shape. Expected direction: if 2026 YTD growth remains positive, August 2026 exceeds August 2025.
candidates.data_to_find: JNTO monthly foreign visitor arrivals for Aug 2019, Aug 2023, Aug 2024, Aug 2025 and monthly Jan–Jul 2026; also Jan–Jul 2025 for YoY. Minimum: Aug 2025 headline, 2026 YTD total and 2025 YTD total.

methods.rationale: Splits August 2025 into China (p35) and non-China (p33-p35), then applies H1 2026 China decline and non-China growth to estimate August 2026. This captures the fact that China was about 30% of August 2025 arrivals, much higher than its H1 2025 average share, so the China collapse drags August 2026 more than the H1 -2.0% headline. Transfer assumption: H1 2026 market-specific growth rates persist into August 2026; no August 2026 market data are available at the cutoff. Failure modes: China decline could ease or deepen, non-China growth could moderate, and August 2025 seasonal mix may differ. Shared dependency: p33/p35 and p60/p58 all derive from JNTO series, so this is not independent of the June trend method.

Uses the June 2026/June 2025 ratio from JNTO preliminary monthly estimates as a proxy for the August 2026 YoY ratio, applied to August 2025. June 2026 total arrivals were 3.15m vs 3,377,985 in June 2025, a decline of about 6.8%. This captures recent total-arrival momentum. Transfer assumption: June's national YoY decline persists through August. Failure: June and August have different market mix; August 2025 had a larger China summer share, so if China remains depressed this method may be slightly optimistic. Shared dependency: p33, p15 and p26 are all JNTO monthly estimates; not independent of m1's JNTO base.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
